description: Machine-readable list of Event.kind values that have been removed from the Cokret v1 protocol. Downstream implementations (SDKs, yougen, soland, cotest) MUST treat these as schema_violation on the wire and MUST NOT introduce them as new contributions. cotest scanner consumes this list to detect drift.

rejection_levels.hard_reject: MUST be rejected at parse/reducer time. No legitimate occurrence on current wire or in current code.
rejection_levels.migration_only: Tolerated only inside offline migration / replay tools, NEVER in current v1 wire parsers. Current parsers (sync, federation, snapshot consumers, reducer, conformance runner) MUST reject the old identifier without inspecting payload shape; migration_tool_only entries carry the `migration_tool_only: true` flag to make this enforceable. There is no in-band reader tolerance window; the prior 'bounded migration window readers MAY tolerate' language has been retired.
rejection_levels.compat_only: MUST appear only on explicitly opt-in interop / compatibility surfaces (e.g., MIMI interop module).
rejection_levels.docs_only: Removed from wire / code; references survive only in CHANGELOG, glossary deprecation notices, or migration guides.

parser_tier_definitions.current_parser: Sync service, federation peer, snapshot consumer, reducer, conformance test runner — anything that processes live or persisted v1 wire bytes. MUST treat every entry in this file as forbidden in input; MUST NOT do payload-shape disambiguation; reject with the schema's standard unknown_kind / unknown_field / schema_violation error.
parser_tier_definitions.migration_tool: Offline batch tool that reads pre-v1 / pre-inversion bytes and rewrites them to canonical v1 form. May consult migration_tool_only entries (those carrying the explicit flag) and apply their disambiguation_payload_shape rule. MUST NOT be embedded in a real-time parser surface (no inline transform; no 'auto-accept legacy and quietly rewrite'). This tier-only allowance is expressed by the `legacy_migration` allowed_context plus, where applicable, the `migration_tool_only` flag — never by a reader-facing tolerance window.

allowed_context_definitions.changelog: May be referenced in spec or downstream CHANGELOG entries documenting the removal.
allowed_context_definitions.legacy_migration: May be referenced only by offline migration / replay tools that translate stored legacy data forward; MUST NOT be consumed by any current_parser surface (sync service, federation peer, snapshot consumer, reducer, conformance runner).
allowed_context_definitions.interop_module: May appear in an explicitly opt-in interop binding (e.g., MIMI interop) where the cross-protocol mapping requires the legacy name.
allowed_context_definitions.negative_test: May appear in negative fixtures / cotest drift tests that assert hard_reject.

entries.notes: Field-level position move was subsumed by track-relative ordering and per-cell ordered_log lattice; no direct replacement.
Bulk field reordering was removed together with cx.field.position.move; ordering authority lives in track / cell lattice.

Track no longer carries independent membership; access semantics derive from the Flow's effective scope. Use cx.member.state at the Realm boundary, or cx.circle.member.state when Flow.scope_circle_id points at an intra-Realm Circle (see zh/models/circle.md). See current-model 'Track 不携带独立 access'.

History visibility lives on the Realm or Circle boundary, not on a track. Use Realm-level history visibility, or Circle-level when Flow.scope_circle_id points at an intra-Realm Circle (see zh/models/circle.md).

Track-scoped read-receipt override is explicitly out of v1 scope (see discovery/read-receipts.md). Read receipts evaluate at the Flow's effective scope: Realm-default or the Circle referenced by Flow.scope_circle_id.
Track-scoped policy components were removed; policy attaches to the Realm boundary, or to an intra-Realm Circle when Flow.scope_circle_id points at one (see zh/models/circle.md).
Lifecycle snapshot event was decomposed into the canonical create / update / upgrade / archive event kinds plus state events; do not re-introduce a single 'set' kind.
Policy snapshot event was decomposed into per-component policy cells (join-policy, history-visibility, delivery-binding-policy, etc.); do not re-introduce a single 'set' kind.

Disambiguation entry, migration_tool_only. The literal wire Event.kind cx.space.create remains an ACTIVE container-shape event. Current parsers (sync, federation, snapshot, reducer, conformance) MUST NOT inspect payload shape and MUST treat any cx.space.create carrying Realm-level fields (security_class / join_rule / history_visibility / policy_server / delivery_binding_policy) as a schema_violation; they MUST NOT reject the current cx.space.create solely by kind string. This entry is ONLY consulted by offline migration / replay tools rewriting pre-inversion bytes to canonical cx.realm.create. See parser_tier_definitions.migration_tool above.

See cx.space.create#pre_inversion_security_boundary for the parser-tier rule: current parsers MUST NOT inspect payload shape and MUST treat any cx.space.update carrying Realm-level fields as a schema_violation; only offline migration / replay tools consult this entry to rewrite pre-inversion bytes to canonical cx.realm.update.

Historical draft event kind 'cx.message.send' was never part of v1 wire. The v1 standard message authoring kind is 'cx.message.create' (see models/common-fields.md). cx.profile.agent_workspace.v1 (and its lite / governed / strict variants) was withdrawn together with the agent_task object, the mirror Realm reservation lattice, and the mention_redirect / import_attestation content blocks. Generic agent participation is still supported through cx.member.state + cx.capability.grant + cx.agent.* protocol session events; private workspaces are deployment-local concerns, not protocol-level.

Current parsers MUST hard_reject the bare names; only offline migration / replay tools (legacy_migration context) translate stored fixture data forward.
